newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-New CEO for merged Metway seen yr-end.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-New CEO for merged Metway seen yr-end.

text.p: Chairman of Queensland's new A$21 billion "mega-bank" John Lamble said a new chief executive of the merged Suncorp-Metway Bank Ltd-Queensland Industry Development Corp (QIDC) would be appointed by the year-end.
"We would hope to announce the new chief executive officer by the end of the year," Lamble told reporters after a Metway shareholders' meeting that approved the merger on Wednesday.

Suncorp Insurance and Finance chairman Martin Kriewald who is also a director of the new bank told Reuters after the meeting three candidates were presently being considered but declined to say whether they were local or overseas.
Lamble also said the merged bank's board had decided to retain the Suncorp and Metway brand names for the time being.
"Bringing them (the brands) together will depend on how well we drive efficiencies through the group," Lamble said.
A new name for the bank and insurance group would not likely to be decided for 12 to 18 months, Lamble said.
Reductions in staff across the three groups would be addressed on a case-by-case basis, as would any branch closures, Lamble said.
The newly-merged group would have more than 5,700 full-time employees with annual attrition rates of about 1,000 annually, Lamble said.
"We are taking staff numbers on a case-by-case basis. We're going to fight hard to limit staff cuts," Lamble said.
About one-half to two-thirds of planned growth would come from cost savings, he said.
The new group was also looking at expansion interstate -- "expansion into New South Wales and Victoria will be maintained and built up," he said.
Lamble said shareholder meetings would have to be held to consider several decisions for the merged group.
"A name change can't be done without a shareholders meeting and directors' fees can't be increased without their approval," Lamble said.
Current directors' fees were those of Metway directors only and the group was now three times larger, he said.
"Current fees do not reflect that," he said.
